lens.message:
Here's the shift: the product is not a phone number — it's curated expertise installation. The phone number/SMS is one distribution channel among several, right in some contexts and wrong in others, so channel choices become fit calls rather than identity statements.

Tanya, verbatim: "The product is not a phone number; it's the phone number distribution channel, and it's the right distribution channel for certain contexts."

What it changes our approach to:
• Product identity and taglines — the old tagline gets superseded, not reworded.
• SMS packaging and tiering — an upsell with real overhead, leaning enterprise, tier mapping deliberately open.
• Demo-channel choice per audience — right where the not-an-AI-chat trust signal pays, wrong where SMS reads as spam-adjacent.
• How experiment claims are recorded — what an experiment asserted stays distinct from what the product is.

Confirm it on one passage — "What this changes about prior canonical content":

As written: The Identity section of the worldview includes the line: tagline: 'The product is a phone number.' This tagline should be superseded. The replacement positioning, in Tanya's voice: 'The product is curated expertise installation. The phone number is the distribution channel for contexts where the trust-signal of "not an AI chat" is worth its operational cost — primarily enterprise.'

Through the shift: the old tagline isn't a slogan due for rewording — it's a category error. An experiment's channel got promoted into standing identity, and it keeps re-embedding because nothing distinguishes what an experiment asserted from what the product is. The product is curated expertise installation; the phone number is one channel among several, worth its verification churn only where the trust signal pays — primarily enterprise — and wrong where SMS reads as spam-adjacent. Every identity statement downstream now has to agree with the replacement line, and the old tagline has to be deleted in the same transaction, not merged in as both-true.
